brannoc.name: Callum - Husky Trickster
brannoc.text: [amused] Nightfall. Running a kitchen? Oh, this I have to taste. Relax — I only brought the good poisons. [long pause] [amused] A cook. Me. Fine — but I'm doing the bitters my way. Nobody dies. Probably.

quell.name: Emma - Wry, Gritty Hero
quell.text: [dry, quiet] I took a vow of silence. I am breaking it to say: your door creaks. Fix it. [long pause] [dry, quiet] I will mind the night desk. Nobody will hear me. That is rather the point.

flint.name: Chad
flint.text: [weary, deadpan] Your bounty's worth eleven silver now. Eleven. I'm here out of pity, mostly. [long pause] [weary, deadpan] I'll keep the books. Somebody in this place should know what things are worth.

marrow.name: Ayla - Bubbly, Cute & Expressive
marrow.text: [excited] We're here to finish the job! — We were never hired for a job. — Then we're here for pie! [long pause] [excited] We'll wait tables! — Both of the tables. — We'll need more tables.

corvina.name: Harriet - Mature British Actress
corvina.text: [haughty] You were hired to end me once. You didn't. Tonight I end your little inn — in print. Two stars. Possibly one. [long pause] [haughty] Five stars. I'll be back every week, and I'll tell everyone. That's a threat, darling.

moss.name: Azgar the Cursed
moss.text: [softly, shy] Boss says break your legs. I'd rather not. Can we just... do the card thing gently? [long pause] [softly, shy] I can sing on Thursdays? And lift kegs. Mostly sing.

rook.name: Harry - Fierce Warrior
rook.text: [frustrated] Twelve years in your shadow, Nightfall. Twelve! You don't even remember my name, do you? It's Rook. Rook! [long pause] [frustrated] Assistant manager. Number two. You know what? It suits me.

oriel.name: Andrea - British female character voice
oriel.text: [mysterious] I foresaw this evening. I foresaw your face. I did not foresee the wallpaper. Bold. [long pause] [mysterious] I'll read fortunes by the fire. Mostly good ones. Business is business.

varr.name: Dusty Garner
varr.text: [firm] Eight years of rooftops, Nightfall. I'm off duty. That doesn't mean I'm not watching. [long pause] [firm] I'll keep the peace on busy nights. Old habits — the good kind.

choir.name: Grav - Deep, Dark & Sinister
choir.text: [whispering] You left us mid-verse, Nightfall. Three voices, one song. Tonight we finish it — with or without you. [long pause] [whispering] Very well. We'll sing on Fridays. All of us. In harmony. You'll regret it.

vesper.name: Elowen - Elf
vesper.text: [earnest] You taught me everything, then you left without a word. I'm not here to kill you. I'm here to ask why. [long pause] [earnest] I bake now. Did you know that? Of course you didn't. Teach me the stew, at least.

mott.name: Alden - Tired Old Man
mott.text: [fussy] You burned down my laboratory. It was already on fire, granted. I've come to settle the ambiguity. [long pause] [fussy] I'll brew tonics. Medicinal ones! I'm reformed. Mostly. Largely.

tally.name: ross
tally.text: [prim] Fourteen years of unfiled returns, Nightfall. Swords are crude. I have paperwork. [long pause] [prim] I'll do your accounts. Somebody must. You keep receipts in a knife drawer.

garr.name: Angus - Calm & Measured
garr.text: [booming] I retired first, Nightfall! I opened a tavern first! Across the street! This town ain't big enough for two reformed killers with a pub. [long pause] [booming] Merge the two? Biggest inn in the five cities. Ha! I'm in.

thorn.name: Beatrice - Mature Female Storyteller
thorn.text: [coldly calm] You were the finest thing I ever made, child. A blade does not get to choose to be a spoon. Come home. [long pause] [coldly calm] ...Then I suppose I'll have the stew.

narrator.name: Eldrin - Wise Epic Fantasy Narration Storyteller
narrator.text: [dry, wry] Once upon a time, the deadliest assassin in the five cities hung up the knives, bought a crumbling inn, and painted a fresh sign. This is not that kind of story. Well. It's a little bit that kind of story. [long pause] [dry, wry] Pair cards that add up to thirteen. Meet them halfway. You used to meet people very differently. [long pause] [dry, wry] Ah. Old habits. Very efficient. Very... you. [long pause] [dry, wry] And just like that, the staff got bigger and the body count stayed exactly the same. [long pause] [dry, wry] They saw the knife work. Trust, like stew, takes time. [long pause] [dry, wry] Word gets around. The Busy Season begins, and so do the visitors who want a word. Or a fight. Usually both. [long pause] [dry, wry] The Grand Reopening. Everyone you ever wronged has accepted the invitation. [long pause] [dry, wry] And here she is. Every story about leaving home ends with someone from home showing up. [long pause] [dry, wry] And so the innkeeper picked up the blade again. The end. Or, as the sequel would put it, the beginning. [long pause] [dry, wry] The sign stayed clean. It turns out the past doesn't get a vote. [long pause] [dry, wry] The inn survived. Its reputation did not. Some stains don't come out with ale. [long pause] [dry, wry] The doors stayed open. Not everyone stayed for a drink. But enough did.
